stem: Meera fixes a straight stick upright in her school playground in Jaipur and marks the tip of its shadow every few minutes. She wants to measure the length of one day, which is nearly 24 hours. Which observation should she use?

options.text: The time between the stick casting its longest shadow on two successive days
The time between the shortest shadow of the stick on one day and the shortest shadow on the next day
The time from sunrise to sunset on a single day
The time between the stick first casting a shadow in the morning on two successive days

teacher.key_rationale: A day is measured from the Sun's highest position to its next highest position; the shortest shadow marks the Sun's highest position (local noon), so the interval between successive shortest shadows gives one day of nearly 24 hours. Longest shadows, sunrise-to-sunset, and first morning shadows do not mark this repeatable noon reference.
